summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Q1 (Indian power-exchange price levels and seasonal patterns relevant to Nepal's exports) and Q2 (existing and planned cross-border transmission capacity) are both PENDING: no value was retrieved. Primary documents located: IEX market-data pages (DAM, HP-DAM, G-DAM, RTM; 15-minute blocks, INR/MWh, exportable), CERC market-monitoring monthly and annual short-term market reports (Excel data), CEA Designated Authority cross-border page, MoP 2018 guidelines and 2021 DA procedure, CEA National Electricity Plan Vol II (Transmission), and NEA annual reports. Method designed: monthly and time-of-day price profile from IEX DAM/RTM/G-DAM (Indian FY April-March) re-aggregated to Nepal FY and to Nepal wet (monsoon) vs dry seasons; capacity recorded line by line with separate thermal rating, operational transfer limit, and approved trading quantum (these differ). Market access is governed by time-limited Indian approvals; search results report 2026 approval events (India-to-Nepal supply approval for Sep-Dec 2026; withheld approval for extending Nepal-Bangladesh trade) - to be verified from CEA/MoP orders.

findings.claim: IEX DAM monthly average and time-of-day (block) clearing prices, April 2022-latest, and the relevant bidding-area price for Nepal-border delivery.
findings.note: Export 15-minute DAM area prices from IEX market-data pages; aggregate to month, to Nepal FY and to wet (approx. June-October) and dry seasons.

findings.claim: Seasonal pattern: price differential between Nepal's surplus (monsoon) months and deficit (dry-season) months, and solar-hours vs evening-peak block differential.
findings.note: Derived from the same IEX series; also CERC monthly reports as cross-check.

findings.claim: G-DAM and HP-DAM price levels relative to DAM (value of hydro as 'green' and peak supply).
findings.note: IEX G-DAM and HP-DAM area price exports; eligibility of Nepali plants for G-DAM to be verified in CEA/CERC rules.

findings.claim: NEA realised export price and import cost by market route (exchange sale, bilateral, Bangladesh trilateral) by FY.
findings.note: NEA annual report energy balance (units in kWh/'units' - convert to GWh) and revenue (NPR); compare with IEX prices for the same months to measure realisation discount (transmission charges, trading margins, losses).

findings.claim: Existing cross-border lines India-Nepal: list, voltage, circuits, thermal capacity, operational transfer limit, commissioning date.
findings.note: CEA NEP Vol II (final), NEA annual report transmission chapter; keep NEA and CEA figures separate if they differ.

findings.claim: Planned/under-construction lines (e.g. New Butwal-Gorakhpur; Inaruwa-New Purnea; Lamki/Dodhara-Bareilly; upgrades of Dhalkebar-Muzaffarpur): capacity, schedule, JV ownership, status.
findings.note: CEA NEP Vol II perspective plan, NEA/POWERGRID JV documents (Oct 2025), Joint Steering Committee minutes; media leads L22 only as pointers.

findings.claim: Approved trading quantum: MW approved by the Indian Designated Authority for Nepali projects on Indian exchanges and for bilateral/trilateral sales, with validity periods; and India-to-Nepal supply approvals.
findings.note: CEA DA approval orders (lead L12); record each approval as a dated observation with MW and validity.

findings.claim: Long-Term Power Trade Agreement (2024) terms and implementation status; Nepal Supreme Court verdict (Nov 2024) on ratification.
findings.note: Official text from MoEWRI/MoFA and the Supreme Court full text; media leads L23-L24 are pointers only.

findings.claim: Nepal wet/dry seasons are defined on the NEA hydrological calendar (to be taken from NEA annual report) rather than calendar quarters; Indian FY (April-March) data are re-aggregated month by month to Nepal FY (mid-July).
Exchange prices are an upper-bound reference for Nepal's export realisation; NEA net realisation is reported separately and the gap is not assumed but measured.

data_gaps: All empirical values (prices, capacities, approved MW, NEA trade volumes/revenue) - no document downloaded in r1.
Final (not draft) CEA NEP Vol II Transmission document URL not yet located; PIB release is a pointer.
CEA Designated Authority approval orders list: page located, individual orders not enumerated.
Amendments to the 2018 cross-border guidelines (reported second amendment; conditions on generator ownership) - texts not located.
Transmission and trading charges (NVVN/PTC margins, ISTS/cross-border transmission charges) needed to convert exchange prices into Nepal-border netback - not located.
Bangladesh trilateral agreement text and tariff - not located.
Bhutan comparator (Bhutan's hydropower export tariffs) for regional context - not located.
units.py has no code for a unit price (INR/MWh, NPR/kWh) or for energy in kWh/MWh; see challenge to 00A.

assumptions.text: Capacity is recorded as three distinct quantities per line: thermal rating, operational transfer limit (N-1 / system-study limit), and approved commercial quantum; only the last constrains trade in the short run.
IEX DAM is the principal price reference; RTM, G-DAM and HP-DAM are reported as sensitivities.
Indian FY and calendar-month data are re-aggregated to Nepal FY using monthly data only; no annual-to-annual splicing.

challenges.text: units.py lacks unit-price codes (e.g. INR_current_per_MWh, NPR_current_per_kWh) and energy codes other than GWh; exchange-price and tariff observations cannot be recorded with a valid unit. Please add. CERC (cercind.gov.in), India Ministry of Power (powermin.gov.in) and PIB are not in the source catalog; propose tier 4/5 entries.

L31 describes CEA approvals as 'import from Nepal' only; the DA also approves India-to-Nepal supply (dry-season imports), which is the other half of X16. Add imports-from-India approval as a separate item.

EXP-06: add approval-renewal risk (time-limited DA approvals, reported 2026 withholding of Bangladesh trade extension - unverified) as a single point of failure for export market access, distinct from physical line capacity; and add dry-season import dependence on the same lines.

NEA energy trade figures are in kWh ('units'); please record GWh with explicit conversion and state Nepal FY. Coordinate on wet/dry season definition so 22B price seasons align with 05A generation seasons.
Opportunity-cost work should use NEA realised netback by route, not IEX clearing prices, as the export value; the IEX series is an upper reference.

Escalation: reported 2026 Indian approval decisions (Bangladesh trade extension withheld; India-to-Nepal supply approval with hour limits) may change S02/S05/S09 assumptions on market access once verified.

uncertainty: High: nothing retrieved. Main structural uncertainties: (i) netback from IEX price to Nepal border is unknown (charges, margins, losses); (ii) exchange prices are volatile and regime-dependent (price caps set by CERC, 2026 fuel shock), so a short history may not represent future export value; (iii) commercial access depends on renewable approvals and Indian policy on generator ownership, which is a discrete political risk rather than a continuous variable; (iv) planned line dates historically slip - completion dates must be recorded as announced vs actual.
